name: server
//version: Deliberately left at 0.0.0 and never bumped: this package is private and never published, and the running version of the product is declared once, by the repository root package.json. One place to bump means two version strings in this repository can never disagree about which build is running.
author: Christian Mariani

scripts.//test: Ends on a sweep, not just starts with one: the daemon-backed passes leave the run's shared registry container up on purpose, so that every file after the first reuses it instead of restarting one. Nothing else is meant to outlive the pass, so the last thing a whole pass does is put the machine back as it found it. The data directory needs nothing here: every test starts from an empty one (test/support/api-lifecycle.ts), so it never holds more than the running test put there.
scripts.test: npm run test:typecheck && npm run lint:list-order && npm run test:unit && npm run test:api && npm run test:sweep
scripts.//VEXEL_DOCKER_LOG: Off for every automated pass. The call log is on by default because an operator running the product is meant to see what it asks of their daemon; a suite is the one reader that is not — a pass makes thousands of calls, and a line each would bury the reporter's own output in the exact place a failure has to be read. The check that covers the log turns it back on around its own calls.
scripts.//run-lifecycle: One entry point behind the four lifecycle scripts below (test/support/run-lifecycle.ts): they used to be four files whose whole body was one call and one log line. The script names are unchanged — test:api, the documentation and a developer's fingers already know them.
scripts.//test:registry: Brings up the run's own registry:2 on this machine and seeds it with every image the tests pull, so that a restore in the middle of a run never reaches a registry on the internet. The seeding is the half that can: an image the daemon does not hold is fetched from Docker Hub once, in order to be mirrored — and every reset opens on that same seeding, so a cold machine pays it on its first reset whether this command was typed or not. Idempotent end to end, so an already-prepared registry is the normal case and one file run directly gets the same arrangement. No pass runs it: there is no global setup on either side, and every file's own reset seeds the same registry directly, so this stays a command an operator types ahead of a run on a cold machine.
scripts.//test:reset-daemon: The per-file reset both daemon-backed passes run, on its own. Destructive to this machine on purpose — it empties Docker except the run's registry — so it is a command an operator types, never one a test file arranges for itself.
scripts.//VEXEL_TIMING_SCALE: Set for the daemon-backed passes and deliberately left unset for test:unit, whose tests pin the shipped cadence values and must keep measuring them.
scripts.//test:api: One file at a time (--test-concurrency=1) because every file drives the same daemon: files in parallel turn contention into failures that say nothing about the product, and a file that stalls stalls behind a wall of unrelated output. The destructive files are in here too, since `prune` acts on the whole host, and they cost the file after them nothing: --import test/support/api-lifecycle.ts empties and re-establishes the daemon before every single file. There is no preparation step ahead of the pass any more — test:sweep, test:images and test:registry used to run first and would only have described a state no file was entitled to assume by the second one; they remain commands an operator can type.
